source_text: Your plan about pattern-to-Rnumber is plausible but I think we could do a bit better.  How about: for each R number, create a fresh codex agent, ask it to read the R-number-associated code (which we have in an interactive figure on "Custom agentic harnesses and memory systems" https://hyperreal.enterprises/about.html) — that will be a priming round.  Then it will bid for patterns from the 150.  We do this via the circa 20 dispatches needed to cover all the R nodes.  Then we collate the bids.  One benefit of doing it this way is that we could get a pattern-based annotation of the code in question if "bid" means "create a Nelson-style hyperlink using code-to-docs" feature in Arxana.

reply_text:
I've mapped the figure (14 R-nodes → Lean modules); now checking Arxana's code-to-docs link format.㊥ (R-node bidding) I think this is better than my plan, and I can set it up. Each R-node gets its own agent, which first reads that node's code and then bids for the patterns it recognises in that code. Each bid is an Arxana link from a code declaration to a pattern. So the bids give us the pattern-to-R-node alignment and, as a by-product, the pattern annotations of the code. Two decisions before I start: whether "fresh Codex" means new seats or fresh sessions on existing ones, and how a bid is stored (last paragraph).

㊢ (what the code side looks like) The harness figure on the about page is `hyperreal.enterprises/harness.html`, built by `p4ng/empirics-futon/gen_lean_dag.bb` from `aif-equations.edn`. It places Lean modules at 14 R-nodes. Two examples:
- R1 is `Proof2.BeliefAtMachine`.
- R6 is `MachinePolicySet`, `Proof2.ContainmentOrder` and `Proof2.PolicyPosteriorAtMachine`.

The rest of the catalogue has no Lean module in the figure: R9, R10, R11, R12, R15, R20, the two CTAU nodes and GRAIN-GATE. For those, the priming pointers would be the Clojure locations given in `control-stages.edn` `:basis` and in the R-node census. That makes 22 dispatches, close to your 20; TRACE is retired.

㊭ (shape of each dispatch) I'd make it one job per R-node, in two steps:
1. **Prime.** The agent reads its node's modules and writes a short account of what the node computes, with each claim citing a declaration at a file and line. I keep that account; it's a record we can check, and it's reusable.
2. **Bid.** The agent sees the top 150 patterns as compact rows: id, stage, title, and the first line of the IF and THEN clauses. It may bid on any pattern, in any stage. A cross-stage bid is a useful check on the stage labels too.
   - **What a bid contains:** the declaration (Lean or Clojure symbol, file, line), the pattern id, and one sentence on how the code does what the pattern's THEN says.
   - **Cap:** at most about 15 bids per agent, so a bid has to be a choice.
   - **No bids:** a valid answer.
   - **Topic patterns:** patterns that are only *about* the node, like `problems/r14-…`, are marked as topic bids.

I collate in code, not by dispatch:
- a pattern with one bidder gets that R-node;
- a pattern with several bidders is listed as one-to-many, with each bidder's citation;
- a pattern with no bidder gets none.

I'd check a sample by opening the cited declaration and reading the pattern's THEN.

🈖 (the Arxana link) This fits Arxana's existing link shape (`futon4/dev/arxana-links.el`). A voiced link goes from a `:code-symbol` source (file, symbol, definition type) to a target, and is stored in futon1 as `arxana/voiced-link`. Two gaps:
- **Target type:** there is no pattern target type yet. Validation only checks that source and target are lists, so a `:pattern` target with the flexiarg path and hash would be accepted. The Arxana browser wouldn't show it until someone adds that.
- **Status:** the allowed values are confirmed, suppressed, orphaned and fuzzy-matched. None of these fits an unreviewed bid.

🈸 (two decisions) First, does "fresh Codex agent" mean new seats? Bringing up a new Codex agent is a terminal step (`codex-picker --new`) that you or I would run 22 times. The alternative is a new session on each idle codex-N, which gives the same clean context with no new seats. Second, should bids go in a file first, with only collated bids promoted to voiced links? Or should every bid be stored directly in futon1 as a link, with a new `:proposed` status added to Arxana? I'd recommend the file first, so 22 agents aren't writing into futon1 at once.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (cross-tab result) The cross-tab says no: within the five loop stages, a turn's pattern stage and its intent stage agree no more often than chance (κ about 0). So intent can't choose the R-node within a pattern's stage. Zai's summary says the intent R-nodes "spread across the stage", but that only repeats which intents are common overall. Of the two options from before, that leaves the direct patterns-to-R-numbers labelling.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I checked) futon0 `4f8f8244`, by zai-1:
- **Files:** the commit has only the four files I asked for. The intent table is parsed from `core.cljs`, not retyped.
- **Join:** it is exact. The pattern row's `turn-id` equals the turn record's `evidence_id`. I matched three turns by hand, and the text, timestamp and pattern line up in each.
- **Coverage:** only 331 of the 4,059 pattern-labelled turns have a 象 reading with an evidence id, nearly all from the last week or so.
- **Tests:** they pass when run as `python3 -m unittest crosstab_stage_intent`. The separate test file is a wrapper that plain `unittest` doesn't pick up, which is untidy.
- **Fixture:** the hand-worked fixture test exercises the matrix and agreement functions, not the join itself.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why the headline numbers need a chance baseline) Zai reports 12.7% agreement, and it compares that to the earlier PBASE check (κ 0.010). But that figure includes assurance, coordination and none turns, which no intent maps to, so they count as automatic disagreements. I recomputed on the five loop stages only, with an expected-by-chance baseline:

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what this suggests) The two labels seem to describe different things about the same turn. The pattern says what the turn is working on, as retrieved from the library. The intent says what kind of conversational move you made, such as reporting, asking or delegating. A "report" lands on PERCEIVE/R2 whatever its subject is. So the intent table describes your move in the conversation, not the War Machine step the turn's subject belongs to. That's worth knowing for the AIF model, since the two could become separate observation channels instead of one being used to refine the other.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(next step for R-numbers) For the patterns-to-R-numbers alignment:
1. Label the functional (practice) patterns only, by reading their THEN clause.
2. Choose only among the R-nodes in the pattern's own stage, with "none" allowed.
3. Go by hits: the top ~150 patterns cover most of the traffic. The 66 existing labels are mostly patterns *about* a component, so they'd be kept separately as topic labels.
4. Check the result against what the agent did next, which is the test the intent table's own notes propose.
